text.p: Reigning world champion Tommi Makinen of Finland took the early lead in the Swedish rally on Friday after the opening stage on a frozen harbour in Karlstad, but the day was dominated by the weather.

An unseasonal warm spell, producing temperatures of five degrees centigrade instead of the usual minus 30 degrees, caused surface ice to melt slightly and left a layer of surface water on the three-km run.

Makinen, who drives for Mitsubishi, stayed out of trouble to set the joint fastest time with Sweden's Tomas Radstrom with main championship rivals, Spaniard Carlos Sainz and Briton Colin McRae, third and fifth respectively.
"It was unfortunate that the weather turned so much of the ice to water, but at least the stage was good for spectators," said Makinen. "I'm happy with my car and very happy to be in first place."
The 169-kms second stage will start early on Saturday morning in Karlstad and will take the teams to Borlange in east Sweden.
Earlier, rally organisers said the event will still be held as planned despite the thaw.
"We have been told that the rally will run as planned," a spokesman for the Subaru team said. "Although there is surface water, there will be no changes to the stages."

German driver Armin Schwarz, fourth in the season-opening Monte Carlo rally, warned: "Without snow, the rally will be much more difficult. You will need an intimate knowledge of the road and it now means that if you make one mistake your rally will be over."
